You Don’t Have to Fight Every Feeling

Anxiety already asks a lot of your nervous system.

What often makes it heavier is everything we add on top of it:

“Why am I feeling this?”
“I should be stronger than this.”
“What’s wrong with me?”
“I need this to stop.”

And suddenly, we’re not only experiencing anxiety—we’re fighting the fact that we’re anxious.

But anxiety isn’t a failure.
It’s a nervous system trying to protect you, sometimes long after the danger has passed.

fullName: Carrie Howard | Therapist for Anxious Overthinkers | TX & FL
text:
Anxiety is NOT all panic attacks & visible freak outs.
It’s the quiet spirals while you nod and smile.
It’s feeling numb as overwhelm tips into dissociation.
It’s pushing past your limits & hiding the exhaustion.
It’s feeling like you’re “too much”… 
While never really feeling good enough.
Anxiety doesn’t always look how you’d expect. ❤️‍🩹
What's something you do to support nervous system regulation?

Music. I have been curating mixtapes/playlists for decades that I use to give me motivation, process loneliness/depression/anxiety, wake up, go to sleep, enhance flow states, promote calm, allow emotional release, etc.
It is both calibration and diagnostic tool for me.

Some nights my anxiety is so loud I can't think. And the thing that quiets it isn't breathing exercises or lists or positive affirmations.

It's remembering.

The back seat of the family car on a long road trip, the hum of the engine, my brother asleep against my shoulder. The weekend at the arcade with my middle school friends, losing track of time over a game we all pretended to be good at.

For some reason, going back there calms me down better than anything designed to calm me down.

What is something a doctor or therapist got wrong about you before your diagnosis?

Called it anxiety for a decade before anyone said the word autism.

Sometimes the best productivity tip is getting enough rest.

Multitasking feels productive. It’s not.

It’s just divided attention dressed up as hustle.

When you focus on one thing. One goal, one task, one move. You go deeper. You think clearer. You finish stronger.

Trying to do everything at once is why nothing gets done right.

Lock in. Cut the noise. Finish what you start.

One target. One mission. No distractions.

If this hit, save it. Share it. Then get back to work.

Wrong.
I didn't have a time problem. I had a management problem.
Fix how you use time before you wish for more of it.
